correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed directly from the injective norm. In the reciprocal-sum-at-most-one region, identity and a diagonal sign map are contractions and their sum and difference are twice coordinate projections. In the reciprocal-sum-above-one region, identity and coordinate swap both have exact norm \(2^{1/p+1/q-1}\); their sum and difference are rank-one maps with exact norm \(2^{1/p+1/q}\), exactly twice as large. The two-dimensional corner embeds isometrically in every \(m,n\ge2\) case, and the universal upper bound \(C_{\mathrm{NJ}}\le2\) closes the proof. Endpoint exponents and the equality boundary are covered by the same formulas. No experiment or partial enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result closes the only parameter gap left by the focal finite-dimensional classical injective theorem and the closest published extension. It turns a collection of sufficient regions into a complete exact classification for every exponent pair and shows that, for this classical finite-dimensional family, the injective/projective distinction visible in the focal theorem disappears at the level of the von Neumann--Jordan constant. The missing region \(1<p,q<2\) is a natural full two-parameter regime, not an arbitrary slice, and the exact witness is structurally transparent.
